tool_description_run_python_node_or_bash: Run Python, Node or bash code in a fresh isolated container. The chat's /workspace is mounted and persists between runs and sessions; everything else is discarded. Network is off unless `network` is true and the chat allows it. Files listed in `export` become artifacts the user can download. Use it for computation, data processing and short scripts; use the Computer for browsing and applications.
tool_description_fetch_a_public_web_page: Fetch a public web page or API response once and return it as readable text: HTML becomes Markdown-like text with links, JSON is indented. With `extract`, return only the values matched by a JSONPath or CSS selector. Internal and private addresses are refused. Use `browser` mode for pages built by JavaScript; use the Computer browser for pages that need login or interaction.
tool_description_draft_deterministic_mon: Draft deterministic monitoring of an API or web page: the URL, what to extract, what to ignore when comparing, child resources to follow and the schedule. Nothing is polled until the operator reviews and publishes the draft. Every change of the observed value becomes a version with a diff and an alert. Test extraction with `web_fetch` first.
tool_description_read_what_an_observe_so: Read what an Observe source recorded: the latest observed value, the list of versions (one per distinct value, with change counts), or the diff between two versions.
tool_description_check_wait_for_or_cance: Check, wait for or cancel jobs that `code_run` or `terminal` returned as `job_id`. Jobs run in parallel and keep running between turns until they finish or are cancelled; results report each job separately. A finished job you have not read is reported to you in a later turn. Waits end early when the user sends a message.
tool_description_work_with_files_in_the_: Work with files in the chat /workspace, which code runs and the Computer share and which persists across sessions. `list` shows a directory, `read` returns text, `write` creates or replaces a text file, `edit` replaces a literal fragment, `export` turns a file into an artifact the user can download (the way to deliver results), `import` writes an artifact, such as a user upload, into a file. Use `write` and `edit` to change files; do not write a program just to save one.
tool_description_use_the_chromium_browse: Use the Chromium browser of the chat's Computer. Runs a batch of steps (navigate, click, type, select, press, scroll, wait, back, tabs, extract, download) and returns each step's result plus a snapshot of the page: visible interactive elements with ids such as `e12`, the visible text and the tabs. Refer to elements by the ids of the latest snapshot; batch several steps when you know them. Downloads go to /workspace/downloads. Prefer this over `screen`; use `screen` for canvas, iframes and applications outside the browser.
tool_description_see_and_control_the_des: See and control the desktop of the chat's Computer (1280x800). `screenshot` returns a JPEG, with element ids of the browser page when `marks` is true; the other actions use the mouse and keyboard at screen coordinates and manage windows. Screenshots need a model with image input. Use `browser` for web pages when it can do the job.
tool_description_run_a_bash_command_in_t: Run a bash command in the chat's Computer, next to its browser and desktop, as the user that owns /workspace and the home directory. A command still running after `wait_s` returns a `job_id` for `job`. Programs with windows appear on the screen. Processes do not survive hibernation of the workspace; files in /workspace do.
tool_description_status_reports_the_chat: `status` reports the chat's Computer and workspace: CPU time, memory against its limit, processes, whether the browser runs and how many terminal jobs, disk use of /workspace and home against its limit, where the workspace is and its last checkpoint, container health (state, out-of-memory kill, restarts) and recent failures. `restart` replaces a Computer that hangs or ran out of memory. Limits are set by the operator; when the work needs more, tell the user.
tool_description_ask_the_user_to_enter_a: Ask the user to enter a login, API key, bearer token or cookie that the task needs. You get a `credential_id`, never the value: pass it to `web_fetch` or to a `browser` `type` step, which send it only to the hosts you named. Never ask the user to paste a secret into the chat, and never put one into code or terminal commands.
tool_description_schedule_a_later_turn_f: Schedule a later turn for yourself in this chat: at the time you name, you get a `wakeup` notice with your reason and can continue the work. A wakeup never interrupts a turn; it waits for the current one to end. Daily and interval limits may postpone it, and it is cancelled if the user turns Proactive mode off.
tool_description_ask_the_user_to_enable_: Ask the user to enable a capability for this chat when the task needs it. Your turn ends while the user decides; if they approve, you continue in a new turn with its tools. If they decline, do not ask for it again: requests for a declined capability are refused until the user changes the chat settings.

chat_this_chat_is_paused_your_messages_w: This chat is paused. Your messages will queue until you resume it.
chat_a_new_message_interrupts_the_agent_: A new message interrupts the agent, and it reads it right away.
approvals_actions_the_agent_wont_take_wi: Actions the agent won’t take without your decision. Requests expire after a day by default.
approvals_when_guardrails_need_your_deci: When a Guardrails rule needs your decision, the request appears here and in its chat.
watch_pages_and_apis_are_checked_on_a_sc: Pages and APIs are checked on a schedule without the agent. You’re notified only when something changes.
watch_add_an_address_yourself_or_ask_the: Add an address yourself, or ask the agent in a chat to watch something. Its drafts wait here for your review.
watch_no_open_alerts_changes_outages_and: No open alerts. Changes, outages and lost access show up here.
watch_new_this_creates_a_draft_nothing_i: This creates a draft. Nothing is checked until you review and publish it.
watch_new_a_public_http_or_https_address: A public HTTP or HTTPS address. Internal addresses are blocked.
watch_new_added_to_every_request_its_sec: Added to every request. Its secret is never shown.
watch_new_a_jsonpath_starting_with_for_a: A JSONPath starting with $ for APIs, or a CSS selector for pages. Empty compares the whole response.
watch_new_compare_this_attribute_of_the_: Compare this attribute of the element, such as href, instead of its text.
watch_new_jsonpath_of_fields_that_change: JSONPath of fields that change without meaning anything, one per line, such as $..updated_at.
watch_settings_credentials_sources_use_f: Credentials sources use for signed-in sites, and where alerts are delivered.
watch_settings_each_new_alert_is_posted_: Each new alert is POSTed as JSON. Failed deliveries are retried. The X-Xavier-Signature header carries t=<unix time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "time.body" with the secret>.
watch_settings_16_to_200_characters_writ: 16 to 200 characters. Write it down now: Xavier never shows it again.
watch_settings_alerts_are_listed_on_the_: Alerts are listed on the Watch page. Add a webhook to have them sent to another system as well.
watch_settings_alerts_stop_being_sent_to: Alerts stop being sent to this address.
watch_source_saving_creates_a_revision_c: Saving creates a revision. Checks keep using the published rules until you publish it.
watch_source_saving_updates_the_draft_no: Saving updates the draft. Nothing is checked until you publish it.
watch_source_checks_are_paused_because_t: Checks are paused because the site rejected this source’s credential. Replace its secret to resume.
watch_source_a_revision_is_waiting_for_y: A revision is waiting for your review
watch_source_this_draft_is_not_being_che: This draft is not being checked yet
watch_source_publishing_starts_checks_on: Publishing starts checks on the timetable shown.
watch_source_checks_stop_and_the_recorde: Checks stop, and the recorded versions, alerts and webhooks of this source are deleted. This cannot be undone.
watch_source_check_requested_a_new_versi: Check requested. A new version appears below only if the value changed.
watch_source_the_resource_was_unavailabl: The resource was unavailable during this check.
watch_source_this_is_the_first_recorded_: This is the first recorded version of this resource in the loaded history, so there is nothing to compare it with.
watch_source_no_versions_yet_the_first_c: No versions yet. The first check records one; later checks add a version only when the value changes.
schedules_work_that_starts_on_its_own_a_: Work that starts on its own: a message to the agent, once or on a schedule.
schedules_run_requested_the_message_appe: Run requested. The message appears in its chat under Work in a moment.
schedules_schedule_a_task_to_have_the_ag: Schedule a task for later today, every morning, or whenever you need.
schedules_no_further_runs_will_start_cha: No further runs will start. Chats it already created are kept.
schedule_new_at_the_chosen_time_xavier_p: At the chosen time, Xavier posts your message to the agent as if you had sent it.
schedule_new_a_new_chat_for_every_run: A new chat for every run
schedule_new_the_first_run_differs_from_: The first run differs from the preview
schedule_new_preview_xavier_xaviers_time: Preview: {a}. Xavier: {b}. Xavier's time is the one that counts.
schedule_new_each_run_starts_a_fresh_cha: Each run starts a fresh chat with the settings below.
schedule_new_each_run_posts_into_this_ch: Each run posts into this chat with its own settings.
schedule_new_choose_at_least_one_thing_t: Choose at least one thing the agent may use.
runs_run_a_short_script_in_isolation_wit: Run a short script in isolation, without a chat. Runs the agent starts are listed here too, linked to their chat.
runs_your_runs_are_listed_here_with_thei: Your runs are listed here with their output and are kept for about a month.
runs_runs_in_a_fresh_container_with_an_e: Runs in a fresh container with an empty /workspace, limited in time, memory and output.
runs_copied_into_workspace_under_their_n: Copied into /workspace under their names before the run.
runs_paths_under_workspace_to_keep_as_do: Paths under /workspace to keep as downloadable files after the run, one per line.
run_the_run_is_still_in_progress: The run is still in progress…
run_not_found_when_the_run_ended_so_not: Not found when the run ended, so not kept:
guardrails_before_the_agent_does_anythin: Before the agent does anything, Xavier checks whether it may. Your rules come first; where you have none, the chat's mode decides. A blocked action never runs, whatever a web page tells the agent.
guardrails_permissions_you_saved_with_al: Permissions you saved with "Always allow" in a chat appear here too. Change one, or delete it to take it back.
guardrails_each_chat_has_a_mode_set_when: Each chat has a mode, set when you start it and changeable in its settings. The mode decides by what kind of action it is.
guardrails_every_action_a_rule_can_be_ab: Every action a rule can be about, and what it touches.
guardrails_each_chats_mode_decides_every: Each chat's mode decides everything. Add a rule to always allow, always ask about, or block a particular action.
guardrails_the_agent_will_go_back_to_wha: The agent will go back to what other rules or the chat's mode say, which usually means asking you.
guardrails_actions_it_covered_fall_back_: Actions it covered fall back to other rules or to the chat's mode, which may be more permissive.
guardrail_new_answer_four_questions_you_: Answer four questions. You will see what changes before anything is saved, and you can change or delete the rule at any time.
guardrail_the_rule_is_replaced_in_one_st: The rule is replaced in one step when you save. Until then it keeps working as it is, and actions already under way are not affected.
usage_what_the_agents_work_cost_in_token: The agent’s work in tokens, money and time. Days are UTC.
account_signed_in_devices_and_api_keys_f: Manage your preferences, password, devices, and API access.
account_used_on_every_device_you_sign_in: Used on every device you sign in to.
account_changing_your_password_signs_out: Other signed-in devices will be signed out. This one stays signed in.
account_this_key_is_shown_only_once_stor: This key is shown only once. Store it somewhere safe—Xavier can’t show it again.
